extracted.intended_audience: patent data analysts, economists and policy researchers using PATSTAT/INPADOC to compute patent indicators
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and variable definitions for computing OECD patent indicators (radicalness, originality, scope, renewal, composite patent quality indices) from EPO PATSTAT and INPADOC data, including algorithms, normalization and dataset structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radicalness index
rubrics_metrics.description: The radicalness index underlines the dispersion of technology classes in the backward citations and the extent to which they differ from the focal patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute distribution of citations by 4‑digit IPC classes and the total number of IPC classes covered in cited patents. OECD provides a T‑SQL implementation: Radicalness = SUM(t1.IPC_Count)/t2.IPC_Total aggregated by citing application, with joins between citation tables and PATSTAT IPC counts; the update only applies where Bwd_Cits > 0 and includes logic to combine EP and WO citation sources. Note: developed by OECD and made freely available for public use subject to acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality index
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality is indicated by a patent combining a wide array of IPC classes; an 'original' patent covers diverse IPC classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original patents (e.g. those in the top quartile of the originality distribution) are also more likely to be radical. OECD shows pairwise correlations between originality and radicalness (around 0.6+ across years), supporting the hypothesis that patents with wide IPC dispersion are more radical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent scope vs cumulative (backward) scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent scope is measured by the IPC content of the focal patent; cumulative (backward) scope is the IPC scope of patents cited by the focal patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IPC counts to measure patent scope (IPC content of focal patent) and cumulative scope (IPC content in backward citations). OECD presents frequency and cumulative distribution charts and correlations to verify whether broader‑scope patents cite patents across a wider array of IPC classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent renewal indicator (length of renewal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent renewal indicator is the simple count of years during which a granted patent has been kept alive — the latest year it has been renewed or until it lapsed or was withdrawn — counted from the application year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to infer private value under the assumption patent owners make profit‑maximising renewal decisions; used to weight patent counts or estimate private value in econometric models. No robustness checks presented because indicator is a simple count. OECD uses INPADOC legal events to identify latest relevant event.

rubrics_metrics.name: INPADOC/EPO event codes for determining renewal/lapse/withdrawal/grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific INPADOC codes and fields are used to determine whether/when a patent was granted, renewed, withdrawn or lapsed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO mappings: Granted EPO patent: Publn_first_grant = 1 (PATSTAT PAT_PUBLN); Renewed EPO patent: prs_code = PGFP (annual fees paid to national office) and latest payment date; Withdrawn: prs_code = 18D or 18W (patent deemed/withdrawn) and date variables; D18D/D18W cancel former 18D/18W if they occur after them (then not considered withdrawn); Lapsed: prs_code = PG25 (lapsed in a contracting state) and earliest date in force. Respect chronology of events per patent when assessing life duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Quality composite index (experimental)
rubrics_metrics.description: A composite indicator designed to capture technological and economic value of patents by combining several patent‑level measures (citations, family size, claims, generality, plus optionally backward citations and grant lag).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OECD proposes experimental indices built on 4 to 6 components, normalised by patent cohort (filing year × technology field) and given equal weights. Caveats: indicator is experimental, suffers from timeliness (citations/grant lag), and results depend on data source, methodology and observation periods. Interpret composite indicators with care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Quality Index (4 components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality index 4 – four components: number of forward citations (up to 5 years after publication); patent family size; number of claims; and the patent generality index. Only granted patents are covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All components are normalised by patent cohort (filing year & tech field) and averaged (equal weighting) to produce the composite index value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Quality Index (4b components, bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality index 4b – four components: number of forward citations (up to 5 years after publication); patent family size; corrected claims; and the patent generality index. Only granted patents are covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variant uses corrected claims instead of raw claims to adjust for potential biases in raw claim counts; otherwise same normalisation and equal weighting approach as index 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Quality Index (6 components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality index 6 – six components: forward citations (as above), patent family size, (corrected) number of claims, generality index, plus number of backward citations and the grant lag index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes measures of cited prior art and examination duration to broaden the quality measure; components normalised by cohort and equally weighted. OECD notes correlation between 4‑component and 6‑component indices declines over time (partly due to truncation affecting grant lag).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward citations (5‑year and 7‑year windows; X/I/Y types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of forward patent citations received within fixed windows after publication: up to 5 years (fw d_cits5) or up to 7 years (fw d_cits7), and variants counting citations flagged as X, I or Y (fw d_cits5_xy, fw d_cits7_xy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as components of composite quality indices and as standalone indicators. Choice of citation window affects timeliness and comparability across cohorts; X/I/Y categorisation allows focusing on substantive/technically relevant citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family size
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent family size (family_size) — number of jurisdictions/patent documents in the patent family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a component of the composite patent quality index; larger families are typically associated with higher value/importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of claims / corrected claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of claims (claims) or corrected claims (adj. claims) in a patent document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims count used as a component of patent quality (more claims often indicate larger protected technological/product space). OECD references literature noting patents with more claims are more likely to be involved in litigation; corrected claims variant adjusts raw claim counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality index
rubrics_metrics.description: Generality index (generality) — a measure of how broadly a patent is cited across different technology fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a component of the composite quality index to capture technological breadth/impact beyond mere citation counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backward citations (count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of backward patent citations (bwd_cits) — count of patents cited by the focal patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used both in radicalness computation (dispersion of cited IPC classes) and as a component in quality index 6. Also used to compute cumulative scope of backward citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant lag index
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant lag (grant_lag) — time elapsed between the filing and grant dates (in days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a component of the 6‑component quality index to capture the length of examination process; subject to truncation and timeliness issues which can affect correlations with other indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakthrough indicator (top 1% highly cited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakthrough flag (breakthrough, breakthrough_xy) — equals 1 if the patent belongs to the top 1% highly cited patents up to 5 years after publication (or when considering X/I/Y flagged citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary indicator used to mark extreme high‑impact patents; can be derived from forward citation distributions within cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑patent literature citations (NPL citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of non‑patent literature citations (npl_cits) included in patent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided as an indicator variable in the dataset; may be used as an additional signal of linkage to scientific literature and as a component in analyses of patent value/quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization by cohorts and cohort statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: All components of the composite indicators are normalised according to patent cohorts defined by filing year and technology field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'cohorts' table provides cohort‑level statistics (mean, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, percentiles 1/10/25/50/75/90/99, min, max, number of patents) used for normalisation and for reporting distributional moments and selected percentiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal weighting of components (methodological choice and caveat)
rubrics_metrics.description: OECD's experimental composite indicators assign equal importance (equal weights) to all components rather than using factor‑analysis weights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice motivated by exploratory analysis showing factor weights differ across technology fields and over time; equal weights improve comparability but are a simplification. OECD notes composite indicators have typical drawbacks and should be interpreted with care; future empirical work may derive optimal coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators dataset structure and variable definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: OECD will make indicators available upon request as tables linked to PATSTAT appln_id; two main tables: 'indicators' (patent document level with non‑normalised indicators) and 'cohorts' (cohort statistics by filing year × technology field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key variables listed include appln_id, filing year, tech_field (Schmoch taxonomy), patent_scope, family_size, grant_lag, bwd_cits, npl_cits, claims, fw d_cits5/fw d_cits7 and XY variants, generality, originality, radicalness, renewal (life duration), quality_index_4, quality_index_6, and others. Note on many_field: when a patent maps to multiple technology fields, the field with majority IPC codes is kept (ties resolved randomly); many_field=1 flags patents allocated to other fields.
